Hi Aditya,

We're seeing a major latency regression in our EU production traffic to Redwood's Hosted API starting ~13:40Z. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms and p99s are spiking above 1.2s. Error rates (5xx) have increased from ~0.1% to ~1.8% and overall TPS dropped ~18% over the last 30m.

This is happening for our EU region only — US traffic looks normal. We rely on steady p95 for our user flows; this is causing timeouts and customer-visible failures.

I've attached a short HAR and service traces from our side (traces_20280115.zip). Can you confirm whether there were any planned changes or known outages? We need an urgent bridge and a rollback plan if this is on Redwood's side.

Please escalate — we're preparing to divert traffic if this isn't contained.

Thanks,
Olivia

Aditya / team — quick technical summary and immediate actions taken: 

What we observed (prelim):
- Around 13:30Z we saw a sudden shift in AS path preference for a subset of EU client prefixes. Instead of terminating at our EU edge pool (eu-edge-2a/b), traffic was advertised/selected via our US egress (us-east-1) resulting in +250–320ms median RTT increase for affected flows.
- BGP dump shows an unintended local-pref bump for the US path originating from a peering config change pushed at 13:26Z by our cloud partner (peering policy id: PEER-20280115-07).
- That hairpin also increased load on US pools causing transient 5xx from overloaded inference workers (hence the error-rate increase).

Immediate mitigations applied (15:00Z–15:10Z):
1) Rolled back the peering policy change at provider (actioned 15:04Z).
2) Pinned HelixHealth prefixes to eu-edge-2a/b via temporary route-map override (15:05Z).
3) Opened emergency steering rule to prefer eu-only pool for HelixHealth customer IDs (15:09Z).

Result: p95 for HelixHealth reduced from 420ms -> ~140ms within ~18 minutes of mitigation; p99 trended down but still noisy while caches repopulate. TPS returned to ~98% of baseline. We are continuing monitoring.

Next steps:
- Full BGP root-cause analysis and reconciliation with provider configs (owner: networking team, ETA: 48h).
- Post-incident rollback validation + test harness for peering policy pushes (owner: infra, ETA: 72h).
- Customer-facing postmortem draft and proposed SLA credit calculation (owner: CS + Sales).

Attachments: bgp_dump_20280115.txt (stripped), p95_metrics_table.csv

Will update as we have confirmation the rollback fully held.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
